methodological_rigor.justification: A rigorous multi-pronged preclinical study combining publicly available human GBM scRNA-seq, internal murine scRNA-seq (CT2A glioma), flow cytometry across four tumor models (E0771, CT2A, Yummer1.7, cLCMV) and two compartments (subcutaneous/intracranial), TNFR2-KO genetic loss of function, adoptive transfer of WT/KO Trp2-TCR-tg T cells in the same host (elegant intrinsic control), bulk RNA-seq with GEO deposition (GSE297330), and pharmacologic validation with a TNFR2 antagonist plus PD-1 blockade with rechallenge experiments. Statistical handling is careful: Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons in survival analyses (alpha 0.0083 for six comparisons), paired/unpaired t-tests as appropriate, two-way repeated measures ANOVA for tumor growth. Minor weakness: n sometimes modest per replicate and power calculations are not specified.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: A preclinical mechanistic study in mice with supporting evidence from human scRNA-seq maps to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is meaningful: identifying TNFR2 as an upstream regulator of TOX and demonstrating that pharmacologic TNFR2 antagonism sensitizes tumors to anti-PD-1 (including in intracranial CT2A-Trp2 where 55% long-term survival and 100% rechallenge protection were observed) provides a concrete translational hypothesis for immunotherapy-refractory tumors like glioblastoma. A clinical TNFR2 antagonist development pathway is plausible but not demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: As a preclinical animal study, ARRIVE is the applicable standard. Most ARRIVE items are addressed: animal source/strain (JAX catalog numbers with RRIDs), age/sex matching (with explicit justification for male-only Yummer1.7 due to female rejection), sample sizes per experiment, randomization is implicit by cage assignment, tumor implantation and endpoint criteria are detailed, statistical approach including Bonferroni correction. Data availability is strong: bulk RNA-seq deposited in GEO (GSE297330), custom R scripts cited, publicly used datasets specified (GSE160189, GSE182109, GSE236243). Minor omissions: formal randomization/blinding statements are not explicitly declared.

novelty_literature.justification: The study makes a specific conceptual advance: TNFR2 is positioned as upstream of TOX in CD8+ T-cell exhaustion progression, emerging temporally after SLAMF6 loss but before TIM3 acquisition, and its loss uncouples TIM3 and TOX expression producing a novel PD-1+TIM3+TOXlo population. The mechanistic link to AP1/NFAT rebalancing and the demonstration that TNFR2 antagonism synergizes with anti-PD-1 in intracranial glioma (a notoriously ICI-refractory setting) are novel. TNFR2 has been studied in Treg biology and proposed as a cancer target by others (refs 34, 35), so the broad concept is not first-in-class, but the CD8-specific upstream-of-TOX framing is genuinely original.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is densely written but logically structured across discovery (scRNA-seq), validation (flow cytometry), loss of function (TNFR2 KO + adoptive transfer), molecular characterization (bulk RNA-seq), and therapeutic translation (antagonist + anti-PD-1 + rechallenge). Figures integrate single-cell, flow, bulk transcriptomics, and in vivo survival curves effectively. Limitations are candidly discussed including the non-memory phenotype of TNFR2-KO T cells despite gain of polyfunctionality, the model-specific absence of tumor control in subcutaneous Yummer1.7, and the multiple TNFR2-expressing cell types that could mediate the effect. Minor typographical errors ('Nfactc2', 'Nfact3') appear in the results text.

key_strengths: Multi-model preclinical validation across four tumor types plus chronic LCMV infection, in both subcutaneous and intracranial compartments, combining human GBM scRNA-seq with mouse scRNA-seq, flow, bulk RNA-seq, and in vivo pharmacology
Elegant mixed adoptive transfer of WT (CD45.1) and TNFR2-KO (CD45.2) Trp2-TCR-tg T cells into the same host demonstrating T cell-intrinsic effect on TOX
Novel conceptual finding: TNFR2 emerges upstream of TOX and uncouples TIM3 from TOX expression, producing a PD-1+TIM3+TOXlo population with hybrid Tex_prog/Tex_term features
Translational pharmacology with anti-TNFR2 + anti-PD-1 achieving 55% long-term survival in intracranial CT2A-Trp2 and 100% protection on rechallenge
Transparent data sharing: RNA-seq deposited in GEO (GSE297330) and code/scripts cited; uses multiple published datasets (GSE160189, GSE182109, GSE236243)
key_concerns: Pure preclinical study without human validation of TNFR2 antagonism
Model-specific heterogeneity: TNFR2-KO did not improve control of subcutaneous Yummer1.7, and the authors do not fully resolve why

Memory phenotype assignment is ambiguous given lack of KLRG1/CD127 changes despite rechallenge protection; the mechanism by which TNFR2-KO T cells form memory-like responses is incompletely characterized
Multiple TNFR2-expressing cell types (endothelial, glial, NK, macrophage) could contribute to tumor control in the KO; cell-type-specific conditional knockout was not performed
Minor typographical errors in gene names (Nfactc2, Nfact3) within the results
chief_reviewer.rationale: A mechanistically novel and thoroughly validated preclinical paper with a credible translational hypothesis and transparent data sharing; tier 1 (e.g., Nature Cancer, Nature Medicine-oncology section, Immunity, Cancer Cell) is plausible at its highest given the multi-model rigor and the therapeutic potential in immunotherapy-refractory GBM.
